findings.claim: The reusable-workflow pins in workflow-selftest.yml are pegged to 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2 (the R1 evidence commit), but the current branch HEAD is f2a674b (the fix-round commit that modified policy-check.yml by adding the fixture-path input). The self-enforcing preflight will detect this stale-pin condition when the PR is submitted and fail with 'policy-check.yml changed in this PR; update both workflow-selftest pins to {head}', blocking merge. Even if the preflight is bypassed, the fixture-pass and fixture-fail jobs call policy-check.yml@76e0f0d which does not declare fixture-path; GitHub Actions would reject the call with an undeclared-input error.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 91 and 187: uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2. dispatcher-result.json git_sha_before == git_sha_after == 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2 (dispatcher ran from 76e0f0d and did not commit). files_changed_self_report in dispatcher-result.json includes .github/workflows/policy-check.yml (change_type: modified). Commit f2a674b ('Slice 020B.1 fix-round R1: close 8 R1 CRIT+MAJ findings') committed these modifications. policy-check.yml at 76e0f0d does not include fixture-path in workflow_call.inputs (that input was added in f2a674b). validate-selftest-config preflight: 'if ".github/workflows/policy-check.yml" in changed and pins[0] != head: raise SystemExit(...)' (workflow-selftest.yml lines 54-57). When the PR is submitted, head = full SHA of f2a674b != 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2, so preflight fires.
findings.impact: The selftest workflow self-blocks: its own CI gate will fail for this PR because the preflight enforces pins == head whenever policy-check.yml changed, and that condition is met. Additionally, at runtime the reusable-workflow call at @76e0f0d would error because the callee at that commit does not declare fixture-path while the caller passes it. Neither failure is a design flaw — both are correct enforcement — but the committed state is inconsistent and requires one more commit to advance the pins to the full SHA of f2a674b before the branch can merge.
findings.mitigation: Update both occurrences of the SHA in workflow-selftest.yml (lines 91 and 187) and both PIN comments (lines 89 and 185) from 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2 to the full 40-character SHA of the current branch HEAD (commit f2a674b). Obtain the full SHA via git rev-parse HEAD before committing. The preflight verify command in the fix-round dispatch-package (verify_commands[2]) will confirm the two pins are equal and both are 40-char hex after the update.

findings.claim: The fixture-tree fallback in policy-check.yml collect-changed-files step uses 'find ${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH} -type f' without filtering by file extension. When 020C adds OPA/Conftest invocation, the fallback will pass non-YAML files such as tests/workflow/fixture-fail/WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md into the evaluation engine. Depending on how Conftest handles non-matching files (parse errors vs. silent skip), this may produce spurious infra errors or unexpected deny findings against .md content.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 212-213: 'find "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort > changed-files.txt'. tests/workflow/fixture-fail/ contains WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md (confirmed by dispatcher-result files_changed_self_report). conftest.md is at tests/workflow/ level and would not be included for per-fixture subtree invocations, but WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md is inside tests/workflow/fixture-fail/ and would be enumerated. When the Conftest bundle runs against this file list in 020C, rule authors must ensure rules are guarded on file extension or explicit filename patterns to avoid .md parse failures.
findings.impact: Forward risk for 020C: if SCP-R-001/002/003 rules do not guard on file suffix, Conftest may attempt to parse WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md as YAML and raise a parse error (SCP-E001 infra failure) or produce an unexpected deny on the fail fixture's fallback run, causing the selftest to fail with a confusing error. The pass fixture does not contain .md files so would be unaffected.
findings.mitigation: Before 020C, add a file-extension filter to the fallback enumerate step: 'find "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" -type f -name "*.yml" -o -type f -name "*.json" | LC_ALL=C sort'. Alternatively, add a guard in the Conftest policy-check invocation (when added in 020C) to pass only recognized file types via --include or explicit file list filtering. Document this constraint in the 020C dispatch package.

findings.claim: The collect-changed-files step outputs changed_files=changed-files.txt via GITHUB_OUTPUT (policy-check.yml line 217: printf 'changed_files=changed-files.txt\n' >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}") but no subsequent step in policy-check.yml consumes steps.collect-changed-files.outputs.changed_files. The file changed-files.txt is used directly by downstream steps in 020C, but the GITHUB_OUTPUT mechanism is unused scaffolding.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 169: id: collect-changed-files. Line 217: printf 'changed_files=changed-files.txt\n' >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}". No subsequent step in policy-check.yml references ${{ steps.collect-changed-files.outputs.changed_files }}. The variable is declared but dead.
findings.impact: No runtime effect. Minor maintenance noise: a 020C implementer adding the OPA/Conftest invocation step might look for this output variable, find it undeclared in the OPA step, and add a duplicate GITHUB_OUTPUT write. Or they might incorrectly believe the file path comes from this variable and fail to pass it correctly.
findings.mitigation: Either remove the printf line entirely and hardcode changed-files.txt in the 020C OPA step, or add a comment noting the output variable is reserved for 020C's OPA invocation step. Prefer removing if 020C will not use the step output mechanism.

findings.claim: The validate-selftest-config pin-freshness check enforces pins == head only when policy-check.yml is in the PR diff. If workflow-selftest.yml is modified (e.g., adding a new job) without touching policy-check.yml, the check does not verify the pin is a real commit SHA in the repository history. A developer could set pins to an arbitrary 40-char hex string and pass the preflight.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 38-43: regex extracts pin SHAs; lines 46-51: checks pins match each other and are both 40-char hex; lines 53-57: only enforces pins == head when policy-check.yml is in changed. No git cat-file or git rev-parse check verifies pin SHA existence in the repository object database.
findings.impact: Very low. If pins are set to a nonexistent SHA, the uses: step fails at runtime with a ref-not-found error. The error is caught, just not at pre-flight time. No security implication.
findings.mitigation: Add a git cat-file -e "${pin}" check in the preflight (after extracting pins) to assert the pinned SHA is resolvable in the local object database. One line: subprocess.run(["git", "cat-file", "-e", pins[0]], check=True) before the changed-files comparison.

findings.claim: The fixture-path isolation fix resolves the scoping problem but introduces a new exit-code chain break: after 020C lands Rego rules, fixture-fail-policy-check will invoke policy-check.yml with default threshold: deny, exit 1 on the deliberately-violating services.yml, and workflow-selftest (which has needs: [stash-fixture-pass-summary, fixture-fail-policy-check] with no if: always()) will be SKIPPED — the comparison step for fixture-fail will never execute. The 020C transition remains non-viable.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:179–188: fixture-fail-policy-check job passes fixture-path: tests/workflow/fixture-fail with no threshold: override; policy-check.yml:14 default threshold='deny'; policy-check.yml:419–422: if effective_denies and os.environ.get('SCP_THRESHOLD')=='deny': sys.exit(1). workflow-selftest.yml:190–196: workflow-selftest job declares needs: [stash-fixture-pass-summary, fixture-fail-policy-check] with no if: always() guard. GitHub Actions: a dependent job is SKIPPED when any needs-job fails. After 020C, fixture-fail/services.yml carries mode.bearer_legacy without valid deprecation date (tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml:14–16) which SCP-R-001 will deny. fixture-fail-policy-check exits 1; workflow-selftest is skipped; the comparison step that asserts fixture-fail's deny findings match the oracle file never runs.
findings.impact: The structural guarantee that fixture-fail produces the EXPECTED deny finding (as recorded in the oracle) is never asserted after 020C. The selftest only confirms that the workflow exited 1 (blocked), not WHICH rule triggered or WHAT finding was recorded. An adversary can modify Rego rule output fields (rule_id, message, remediation_url) or the bypass_emitted flag without the oracle comparison catching it. The CG-CRIT-01 closure report from fix-round-1 is premature: scoping is fixed, but the comparison chain is still broken after 020C.
findings.mitigation: Option A — add threshold: warn to both fixture invocations in workflow-selftest.yml; the job exits 0 even with deny findings, the comparison chain completes, and the oracle comparison asserts the correct deny output. A separate step (or the comparison step itself) asserts that fixture-fail's actual findings array contains at least one deny-verdict entry. Option B — add if: always() to the workflow-selftest job and change its needs: to use needs.fixture-fail-policy-check.result == 'failure' || needs.fixture-fail-policy-check.result == 'success' logic; this is fragile in GitHub Actions YAML. Option A is cleaner. Must be implemented before 020C opens.

findings.claim: The selftest comparison validates summary JSON content but not threshold-enforcement exit behavior. An adversary can remove sys.exit(1) from the Render-deny-annotations step of policy-check.yml, update the SHA pin to satisfy the preflight check, and the selftest will not detect the removal: the comparison passes because findings still appear in the JSON summary, but the required-status check no longer blocks PRs on deny findings.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:419–422: the sole enforcement point is `if effective_denies and os.environ.get('SCP_THRESHOLD')=='deny': sys.exit(1)`. workflow-selftest.yml:220–268 (Compare reusable-workflow summaries): normalize() extracts schema_version, rule_set, findings, disabled_rules, waivers_applied, bypass_emitted, conflict_gate — no assertion on job exit code. If sys.exit(1) is removed, the workflow produces an identical summary (deny findings still recorded in JSON) and exits 0; fixture-fail-policy-check exits 0; workflow-selftest runs and compares; normalize(actual)==normalize(expected) passes. validate-selftest-config enforces that if policy-check.yml changed then pins==HEAD; the attacker satisfies this by updating both pins to their malicious commit HEAD. After 020K adds CODEOWNERS on .github/workflows/**, this attack requires a CODEOWNER approval, but in 020B.1 no CODEOWNERS exists.
findings.impact: After 020C adds Rego rules and 020D2 enables the required check, a PR that modifies policy-check.yml to remove threshold enforcement (removing six lines at policy-check.yml:419–422) while keeping summary JSON generation intact will pass the selftest and, subsequently, will cause scp/policy-check to always exit 0 — allowing any PR with any policy violation to merge. This is the highest-value attack on the primitive: it neutralizes the enforcement without altering the observability surface. The self-reported concern from R1 about this scenario remains unaddressed.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit exit-code assertion to the selftest harness: after 020C, the fixture-fail-policy-check job (or a wrapper step around it) should be expected to exit 1, and workflow-selftest should assert the job outcome was 'failure'. Implementable by adding a step to workflow-selftest that reads the needs context: `if [ '${{ needs.fixture-fail-policy-check.result }}' != 'failure' ]; then exit 1; fi`. This requires workflow-selftest to have if: always() (see R2-SBP-MAJ-01). Alternatively, add a canary assertion in the comparison step: for the fixture-fail case, assert that actual['findings'] contains at least one entry with verdict=='deny' AND assert that a downstream wrapper invocation of policy-check.yml with the same fixture-fail input would exit non-zero — the latter requires a dedicated canary step. The combination of R2-SBP-MAJ-01 (if: always()) and this finding (exit-code assertion) must be addressed together.

findings.claim: The fixture-path input validation accepts relative traversal paths (../) and absolute paths (/etc) because the Python guard only rejects empty strings and three control characters (\n, \r, \x00). The subsequent existence check `[ ! -e "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" ]` passes for any existing filesystem path, including parent-directory traversals. The fallback `find "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" -type f` would enumerate files outside the repository root.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:190–199: Python check: `sys.exit(0 if value and all(ch not in value for ch in ('\n','\r','\x00')) else 1)`. policy-check.yml:201–203: bash existence check: `if [ "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" != '.' ] && [ ! -e "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" ]` — passes for `../`, `../../`, `/tmp`, etc. policy-check.yml:213: `find "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH}" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort > changed-files.txt` — traverses the supplied path. In the selftest context the paths are hardcoded (tests/workflow/fixture-pass, tests/workflow/fixture-fail) and not attacker-controlled. For downstream callers of the reusable workflow, fixture-path is set via the calling workflow YAML (checked-in code) so exploitation requires modifying the caller's workflow file.
findings.impact: Not directly exploitable in the selftest context. For general callers, a misconfigured or compromised calling workflow with fixture-path: ../.. would cause OPA evaluation to scope to the repo root parent, potentially evaluating files outside the repository. The more practical concern: a caller with fixture-path: tests/../../.scp or similar could unintentionally (or intentionally) scope evaluation to a non-fixture directory, producing unexpected findings or no findings at all (silencing policy enforcement for that invocation). Defense-in-depth gap.
findings.mitigation: Add path validation in the collect-changed-files step: reject any fixture-path that (a) starts with / (absolute), (b) contains the substring ../, or (c) resolves via realpath to a location outside the repository root (compare against git rev-parse --show-toplevel). Python guard: `import os; path=os.path.realpath(value); root=os.path.realpath(subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','--show-toplevel'],text=True).strip()); assert path.startswith(root+os.sep) or path==root`. This closes the traversal gap without restricting legitimate deep subtree paths.

findings.claim: The ratchet anti-bypass check (validate-selftest-config) uses git diff --name-only base..head WITHOUT the -- path-scope argument, meaning it computes the full PR diff across all files. While this is correct for the ratchet purpose, the same subprocess also serves as the input to the SHA-pin check (policy-check.yml in changed). A PR that adds a file named .github/workflows/policy-check.yml outside the repo root via a submodule or nested workspace would cause policy-check.yml to appear in changed without actually modifying the reusable workflow, triggering the SHA update requirement spuriously.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:49–57: `changed = subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only',f'{base}..{head}'],text=True).splitlines()` — no path filter. Line 54: `if '.github/workflows/policy-check.yml' in changed and pins[0] != head`. Line 49: same changed list used for ratchet check (lines 67–81). The string `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` matches any file at exactly that relative path. In a repo with a submodule or worktree that has its own .github/workflows directory, a diff of the submodule pointer would not include the inner path — this case is benign. However, the concern is the inverse: the changed list is populated from git diff output which could contain paths like .github/workflows/policy-check.yml from other contexts (e.g., renamed files, merge commits with unusual diff output).
findings.impact: Low probability in practice. No direct bypass scenario; this would cause a false-positive enforcement (requiring SHA update when policy-check.yml didn't actually change) rather than a bypass. However, in the opposite direction: if git diff output ever OMITS .github/workflows/policy-check.yml from changed (e.g., due to submodule diff elision), a PR that genuinely changes policy-check.yml would pass the SHA check without updating the pin — the same stale-SHA false-green risk from R1-SBP-002. fetch-depth: 0 in workflow-selftest.yml mitigates shallow-clone elision.
findings.mitigation: Scope the git diff for the SHA-pin check to explicitly target the workflow file: `subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only',f'{base}..{head}','--','.github/workflows/policy-check.yml'],text=True).strip()` and check if output is non-empty. This is more precise than string-matching against an unsorted full-diff output. Keep the full diff for the ratchet check (which genuinely needs to scan all fixture paths).

findings.claim: R1-SBP-004 carry-forward: fixture-pass/services.yml uses jwks_url: https://example.com/.well-known/jwks.json. If SCP-R-001 (020C) validates jwks_url domain beyond URI-format-only, example.com will produce a deny finding on the fixture-pass fixture, breaking the selftest permanently after 020C merge.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/fixture-pass/services.yml:16: jwks_url: https://example.com/.well-known/jwks.json. tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml does not carry jwks_url (mode.bearer_legacy shape, lines 14–16). WP-SCP-020 §4 020C: SCP-R-001 validates root-shape conformance to pre-D-021 SVC-003 mode set; sub-field validation scope of jwks_url not specified. No note in conftest.md or WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md. Unresolved since R1.
findings.impact: If SCP-R-001 validates jwks_url domain pattern (e.g., must match *.brokapps.ai), fixture-pass permanently fails after 020C, blocking all downstream slices. Forward-commitment risk.
findings.mitigation: Before 020C opens: document in the SCP-R-001 rule spec whether jwks_url is validated for format-only or also domain. If domain validation is in scope, replace example.com with a value that will always satisfy the rule. Add a note to conftest.md.

findings.claim: R1-SBP-005 carry-forward: tests/workflow/** is absent from the planned CODEOWNERS path list in slice 020K. After 020C promotes fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json to contain real deny findings, that oracle has no designated-reviewer gate at PR merge time.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list: policies/**, renovate/**, .github/workflows/**, docs/DECISIONS.md, output/findings/waivers.json. tests/workflow/** absent. No CODEOWNERS file exists in repo. Combined with the oracle-from-HEAD read (expected-annotations.json loaded from working tree in normalize()), this means any contributor can weaken the oracle between 020C and 020K without a reviewer gate. Unresolved since R1.
findings.impact: Window of exposure from 020C merge to 020K landing (multiple slices). Single-file oracle change (expected-annotations.json only) is blocked by the selftest comparison (actual≠expected), but a compromised contributor with understanding of the system could craft a scenario. Primary concern is governance continuity: no human review layer compensates for the structural tautology gap during this window.
findings.mitigation: Add tests/workflow/** to 020K CODEOWNERS. Flag the gap in conftest.md so the 020C author is aware.

findings.claim: R1-SBP-007 carry-forward: the stash-rename-delete artifact ceremony between fixture-pass and fixture-fail invocations still relies on artifact API propagation with no post-delete verification. The per_page=100 pagination fix (COR-003) was applied, but the fundamental eventual-consistency fragility is unresolved.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:117–177: stash-fixture-pass-summary job deletes the artifact named policy-check-summary after renaming it. No sleep or re-list verification after the DELETE 204. Per_page=100 is now present (line 131). The DELETE-then-upload race between jobs is sequenced by the needs: chain but propagation latency is not explicitly gated. Unresolved since R1.
findings.mitigation: Eliminate ceremony by adding artifact-name-suffix input to policy-check.yml so each invocation uploads to a distinct name directly. Deferred to a later slice if not blocking 020C.

findings.claim: CG-MAJ-02 from R1 is not closed in the governance canonical: plan §4 020B.1 still lists only three trigger paths (.github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**) and omits schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json. No tracked remediation item (BACKLOG row or future-slice requirement) exists to ensure the plan is ever amended.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B.1 row: 'SCP-local job workflow-selftest trigger = pull_request on paths .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/** (blocks merge of any PR touching those paths).' — three paths only. .github/workflows/workflow-selftest.yml lines 5–9: paths: .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**, schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json — four paths. Fix-round dispatcher-result.json self_reported_concerns: 'docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md was outside the allowed write scope, so the schema-trigger rationale was documented in the in-scope dispatch artifacts rather than in the parent plan row itself.' No BACKLOG.md entry, no future-slice reference in any committed plan document names this gap as requiring resolution.
findings.impact: The plan §4 020B.1 row is the governance canonical for 020B.1 conformance audits. Every subsequent reviewer comparing implementation to plan spec will find an undocumented trigger path. More critically: an implementor following only the plan to recreate or extend the selftest trigger set would omit schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json, creating a CI blind spot where schema changes bypass the selftest gate. The gap is live through all remaining WP-SCP-020 slices since no remediation is scheduled.
findings.mitigation: Amend plan §4 020B.1 trigger-path row to add schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json with rationale '(expected-annotations.json is schema-bound; schema changes must re-validate all fixture expectations)'. This is a one-line documentation edit. It can be combined with the fixture-path input amendment required by R2-CMP-MAJ-02 into a single plan-amendment commit. Open a BACKLOG item or add a pre-dispatch requirement to 020C to confirm this edit lands before 020C review checkpoint.

findings.claim: The fixture-path input added to policy-check.yml during fix-round R1 is not reflected in plan §4 020B AC (i) input enumeration. Plan §4 020B AC (i) is the canonical deliverable specification for the reusable workflow's input surface; it enumerates exactly six inputs. The implementation now has seven. No plan amendment was made and none is scheduled.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B AC (i): 'inputs: enumerated with type: — rule-set: string (default: "starter"), threshold: string (default: "deny"), annotate: boolean (default: true), scp_bypass: boolean (default: false), waivers-path: string (default: "output/findings/waivers.json"), rule-config-path: string (default: ".scp/rule-config.yaml").' Six inputs only. .github/workflows/policy-check.yml lines 6–40: seven inputs, including fixture-path: string (default: '.') at lines 37–40. Fix-round dispatch package scope_boundary excluded docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md. Executor self_reported_concerns acknowledge the plan was out of write scope; no tracked remediation item exists. WP-SCP-020 §9 AC 6 ('workflow-selftest green on pass + fail fixtures') implicitly depends on fixture-path being present, but the AC text makes no mention of it.
findings.impact: A post-WP completeness audit comparing implementation to plan §4 020B AC (i) will flag fixture-path as undocumented scope. More critically, downstream adopters reading the plan for the canonical input surface will not see fixture-path and may not know it exists. Adopters who want to scope policy evaluation to a subdirectory (a valid use case given the input's default-'.'-semantics) have no plan-level pointer to this capability.
findings.mitigation: Amend plan §4 020B AC (i) to add 'fixture-path: string (default: ".") — restricts changed-file discovery to a path prefix; defaults to whole-repo evaluation for normal callers; used by the selftest harness to achieve fixture-tree isolation.' This amendment can be batched with the R2-CMP-MAJ-01 trigger-path fix into a single plan edit commit before 020C opens.

findings.claim: Oracle tautology (020B1-SBP-001) is closed for same-PR co-edits but a staged two-PR attack remains viable post-020C. The compensating control — CODEOWNERS on tests/workflow/** — is deferred to 020K but is not enumerated in plan §4 020K's CODEOWNERS path list, so there is no governance guarantee it will land there.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 67–81: ratchet check guards only the case where services_path in changed AND expected_path in changed AND exists_at(base, services_path) AND exists_at(base, expected_path). A staged attack: PR-A changes only fixture-fail/services.yml to a compliant shape (passes ratchet, changes only one of the pair); PR-B subsequently changes only fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json to empty findings (passes ratchet, only one of the pair). After both PRs merge, fixture-fail expects empty findings and services.yml is compliant — selftest passes, oracle is neutralized. docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list: 'policies/**, renovate/**, .github/workflows/**, docs/DECISIONS.md, output/findings/waivers.json' — tests/workflow/** is absent. The R1 review noted tests/workflow/** must be added to 020K scope; this has not been acted on.
findings.impact: From 020C merge (when fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json contains real deny findings) until 020K merge (when CODEOWNERS is wired), anyone with write access to the repository can execute the two-PR staged attack without a designated-reviewer gate. The window spans at least slices 020C through 020J — several months of exposure. After 020K, the attack still requires CODEOWNERS approval of both PRs, which is a strong compensating control, but only if tests/workflow/** is in the 020K CODEOWNERS list.
findings.mitigation: Add tests/workflow/** to plan §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list explicitly: 'tests/workflow/** — oracle files for the selftest harness; mutations require named-reviewer sign-off.' Add a note to conftest.md: 'Note: tests/workflow/** will be covered by CODEOWNERS in slice 020K. Until that slice merges, oracle file changes require manual review discipline.' This ensures the 020K implementor does not overlook the path.

findings.claim: fixture-fail/services.yml contains the field waiver_ref: W-020B1-SELFTEST which is not a field defined in the SVC-003 mode-set accepted_modes schema, is not documented in conftest.md, and has no corresponding waivers document anywhere in the repository. If SCP-R-001 (020C) validates accepted_modes entries strictly (no additional properties), this field will cause an unexpected deny finding on a different rule violation path than the one the fixture is designed to test.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml lines 14–17: accepted_modes entry is {mode: mode.bearer_legacy, deprecation_close_date: '2099-12-31', waiver_ref: W-020B1-SELFTEST}. docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020C: SCP-R-001 validates 'services.yml root-shape conformance to pre-D-021 SVC-003 mode set (mode.user_oidc, mode.service_rs256, mode.api_key, mode.bearer_legacy); deprecation_close_date ∈ {"2026-06-30", "2026-09-30"}.' The plan does not enumerate waiver_ref as a valid field. No waivers.json or DECISIONS.md entry references W-020B1-SELFTEST. conftest.md does not mention waiver_ref or explain its purpose. Fix-round dispatcher-result.json: 'Pre-positioned the fail fixture with a future-rule violation shape' — no mention of waiver_ref.
findings.impact: If SCP-R-001 validates accepted_modes entries with additionalProperties: false (a common strict-schema pattern), the waiver_ref field will trigger a deny finding with a message about unexpected field rather than about mode.bearer_legacy deprecation_close_date. This makes fixture-fail's deny summary ambiguous — it fails for the wrong reason — and the 020C transition would require fixing the fixture-fail shape rather than just flipping expected-annotations.json. The pre-positioned forward-reference to W-020B1-SELFTEST also creates a false impression that a waiver for this fixture already exists.
findings.mitigation: Either (a) remove waiver_ref from fixture-fail/services.yml and add a YAML comment: '# mode.bearer_legacy with out-of-range deprecation_close_date: SCP-R-001 will deny this once 020C ships'; or (b) confirm in conftest.md and the 020C dispatch package that SCP-R-001 will not validate waiver_ref (because it is at the mode-entry level and the rule only checks mode and deprecation_close_date fields). If (b), add a note to conftest.md explaining waiver_ref is a non-enforced annotation. Resolve before 020C dispatch opens.

findings.claim: The fixture-path input description in policy-check.yml implies the input is only for selftest harness use, which misrepresents it as a general-purpose scoping mechanism available to any caller.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 37–40: description: 'Restrict changed-file discovery to a fixture subtree when the selftest harness invokes the workflow.' The phrase 'when the selftest harness invokes the workflow' scopes this as a harness-only feature. Default is '.' and the validation logic is general-purpose: any caller could pass a subdirectory to scope evaluation. ADOPT-001 §12 (planned in 020H part 3) will document the input surface; if this description ships as-is, adopters who read it will not recognise the subdirectory-scoping capability.
findings.impact: Low. No runtime regression. An adopter wanting to scope evaluation to a monorepo subdirectory would not discover this input from its description. The capability exists but is undiscoverable.
findings.mitigation: Rephrase the description: 'Restrict changed-file discovery to a path prefix. Defaults to "." (whole-repository evaluation). Set to a fixture directory path when invoking from a test harness, or to a subdirectory when the caller wants to scope evaluation to a monorepo package.'

findings.claim: The oracle ratchet's asymmetric treatment of new versus existing fixture pairs is undocumented in conftest.md. New fixture pairs may freely set both services.yml and expected-annotations.json in one PR; existing pairs may not. A contributor adding a new fixture pair will not know this asymmetry or its governance implication (new pairs start with weaker oracle protection).
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 73–80: ratchet condition includes exists_at(base, services_path) AND exists_at(base, expected_path). A new fixture pair has neither file at base, so exists_at returns False for both; the ratchet is bypassed. conftest.md documents the ratchet behavior ('Existing fixture pairs are ratcheted: a PR may not change both services.yml and expected-annotations.json for the same committed fixture in one change') but does not call out the new-pair exception.
findings.impact: Very low. Design-correct behavior for bootstrapping new fixtures. However, a future contributor introducing a low-quality new fixture pair with a trivially-passing expected oracle would not be warned that their pair starts unratcheted until the next review cycle flags it.
findings.mitigation: Add one sentence to conftest.md after the ratchet description: 'New fixture pairs introduced for the first time may include both files in one PR; the ratchet applies only to pairs that already exist at the PR base.'
